rules.instruction: When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.
rules.situation: the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process

rules.instruction: When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.
rules.situation: the description states a specific activity purpose, meaningful qualifier, or completion outcome for a BPMN element

rules.instruction: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.
rules.situation: the description states an activity or outcome together with its purpose, result, or alternative forms

rules.instruction: When the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives: Model each activity as a separate task on its own branch rather than combining the alternatives into one task; choose a gateway that matches whether one or multiple alternatives may be performed.
rules.situation: the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternative ways to achieve an outcome

rules.instruction: When the description presents multiple alternative ways to perform one activity: Label the BPMN activity at a level of generality that preserves the alternatives rather than selecting only one.
rules.situation: the description presents multiple alternative ways to perform one activity
